# Evidence digest (generated by scripts/build_ledger.py — summaries, open questions and takeaways of every stream)

# E00-source-identity.md


# E01-genesis.md

## Open questions / uncertainties
- How `16941f7198` (42k lines, 596 tests, about 2h50m after init) was produced is not stated anywhere in the repo. It has no trailer, the term "one-shot" is never defined, and no prompt or spec is committed. AI involvement for the first 10 commits is UNKNOWN.
- Contents of the private `plan/` (research, parity plan, execution plan, estimates), `log/devlog.md` and `craftrules` cannot be observed. Referenced but missing: `rust-framework-options.md`, `photon-studio/06-menu-snapshot.md`, `photoshop-parity.md`.
- Trailers name inconsistent models (Opus 5.5 vs 4.8 on related work, E01-012). Their accuracy as a model record cannot be checked.
- The "8 parallel agents" figure (E01-014) is self-reported. No per-agent identities exist in the first-week founder commits.
- Issues #1–#7 etc. come from a WebFetch summary only (lower fidelity). PR open/merge times were not fetched.
- The v0.4.x versions were never tagged, so the release history for 0.4 is unclear.
- Rust LOC is a raw line count (includes comments and blanks), not cloc.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Make the agent guide (AGENTS.md) a day-0 artefact. Put the architecture invariants, a "before you finish" checklist and parallel-agent rules in it from the first code commit (E01-003).
- Encode the target product's feature surface as data, generate a parity checklist from it, and ratchet with a never-lower FLOOR (E01-015).
- Then demote breadth metrics explicitly once they saturate, in favour of an "honest assessment" that agents must read first (E01-019).
- Give parallel agents mechanical isolation rules: a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent, file ownership, a new module per area, atomic manifest writes, and "don't fix others' in-progress files" (E01-003, E01-016).
- Plan for abrupt session ends: a dev log plus an always-green tree as the agent hand-off protocol (E01-016). Note the drawback: here the log is private.
- Enforce layering and portability in tooling (`cargo xtask layers`, wasm check) from the first CI file, not only in prose (E01-002).
- Turn observed failure classes into numbered rules backed by a test (panic_hunt). Then fan the fix out as per-crate PRs (E01-027).
- Put shared cross-project standards (release, licensing, never-crash) in a sibling rules repo. But keep cited rules reachable for outside contributors, which caused friction here (E01-023).
- Use generated, CI-checked scorecards (`--check`) instead of hand-edited status docs (E01-018).
- Ship release automation on day 2, so frequent tagged releases (v0.1→v0.5 in 8 days) are cheap (E01-024).
- Record AI involvement with explicit trailers from early on. Watch for model-name drift that weakens the record (E01-011, E01-012).
- Planning before code existed but stayed private (gitignored `plan/`). For auditability, commit the spec or plan, or a redacted version (E01-005).


# E02-agent-instructions.md

## 0. Summary

- `AGENTS.md` is the only agent-instruction file on `main` at the repository root. It is 24,989 bytes and
  214 lines (`wc -c`, `wc -l`). It has **38 revisions** (`git log --follow --format=%h -- AGENTS.md | wc -l`),
  from `16941f7198` ("one-shot", 2026-09-30) to `0d9a9a5a70` (2026-11-11).
- Since `7d8648dfcb` (2026-11-06, PR #11632), lines 1–52 are two machine-checked blocks copied from the
  organisation repo `storytold/craft-contrib`: **House rules** (15 rules) and **Rust Craft repositories**
  (6 rules plus the licence allowlist). Each block carries a sha256 in its header. I recomputed both hashes
  and both match (E02-012). The CI workflow `house-rules.yml` triggers on changes to `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.cursor/` and nested example `AGENTS.md` files exist **only on unmerged PR
  refs** (forks). None has ever reached `main`. On `main` there are also `docs/user/AGENTS.md` and a
  one-line `docs/user/CLAUDE.md`.
- No PR template, CODEOWNERS, `.mcp.json`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or `.codex/`
  exists on any ref I searched (E02-020).
- The documented agent workflow covers these points:
  - parallel agents use separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`s;
  - state is handed between sessions through a gitignored `log/devlog.md` plus a green tree;
  - work is picked from ranked docs (`docs/gaps.md`, `docs/scorecard.md`);
  - estimates are stated in "Opus 5.5 agent-hours";
  - a stop-and-ask list exists (releases, licensing, secrets, destructive git, …);
  - "No agent attribution" in PRs (house rule 15, since 2026-11-06). Meanwhile the About window credits
    AI models from `Co-Authored-By` trailers.

---

## Open questions / uncertainties
- The contents of the external reusable workflows (`craft-common-actions` house-rules.yml and gate.yml)
  are not in the clone. So it is unknown:
  - what exactly the house-rules check verifies (presence, position, hash, source sha);
  - whether gate.yml checks licences.
- Branch-protection settings and required-review counts are not visible in git.
- The private `craftrules` standards, and the local `plan/` and `log/devlog.md`, are unavailable. The main
  inter-session memory artefact cannot be examined.
- Why `plan/` "do not ask / do not stop" was added: no incident commit was found (E02-010 is INFERRED).
- craft-contrib rule 15 wording was seen only via a WebFetch summary, which paraphrased it inconsistently.
  The local hash-verified copy is used instead.
- Whether the PR-only agent configs (#11086, #5433, #8540, #6479) were closed or merely left open was not
  checked (no API access; WebFetch was not run for each).
- Decision #4779's disappearance from decisions.md: the side-branch history was not fully traced.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Keep one agent-instruction file (AGENTS.md) as the canonical entry point. Point other tool-specific
  files (CLAUDE.md) at it rather than duplicating it (E02-001, E02-021).
- Document a new mechanical gate in the agent guide in the same PR that builds it, so the definition of
  done tracks the tooling (E02-005, E02-006).
- Pair a prose rule with an executable check (clippy deny, `panic_hunt`, `xtask layers`,
  `panel-commands`). Rules with no check (licence allowlist, rule 15, claim-before-coding) are the ones
  practice diverges from (§4, E02-016).
- Spell out concurrency etiquette for agents sharing one checkout: per-agent `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, file
  ownership, new modules instead of shared-file growth, atomic manifest writes, "wait and retry, don't fix
  their files" (E02-003).
- Make session hand-off explicit: a terse devlog entry plus an always-green tree, justified by "context
  limits" (E02-004). The project keeps this log out of git, which hides it from collaborators; a fork chose
  in-tree instead.
- Give agents a ranked, machine-readable work queue, and have them update its evidence when they move a
  number (E02-007).
- Plan in agent-hours, and label what a human must do (E02-008).
- Write a short, closed stop-and-ask list plus an anti-stall rule ("do not ask for it and do not stop") so
  autonomous agents neither over-escalate nor take irreversible actions (E02-009, E02-010).
- Share rules across sibling repos as hash-verified blocks sourced from one public repo, and check them in
  CI. A private shared-rules repo failed for outside contributors (E02-012, E02-013).
- Close the loop from bot review to the rules: CodeRabbit findings led to precise rule wording (E02-015).
- Decide the attribution policy explicitly. Here the "no agent attribution in PRs" rule coexists with a
  product feature that credits models from commit trailers (E02-011, E02-017).


# E03-git-quant.md

## 0. Reproduction

```bash
UPSTREAM=<scratch>/upstream/photocraft          # read-only clone, PR heads fetched
python3 scripts/e03_git_quant.py "$UPSTREAM"    # ~30 s; writes data/E03_*.csv (43 files), prints a report
python3 scripts/e03_growth.py   "$UPSTREAM"    # ~7 s;  writes data/E03_growth.csv, data/E03_growth_crates.csv
```
Both scripts: Python 3 stdlib only, optional `--pin SHA`, read-only on the clone.
Core extraction (in `e03_git_quant.py`):
`git log <PIN> --no-renames --numstat --format=%x1e%H%x1f%P%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%aI%x1f%cn%x1f%ce%x1f%cI%x1f%B%x1f`,
`git rev-list --first-parent <PIN>`, `git log <PIN> --no-merges --no-renames -p -U0 -- '*.rs'` (test attributes),
`git for-each-ref refs/pull refs/remotes/origin refs/tags`.
Growth (`e03_growth.py`): `git ls-tree -r -l <snap>` + `git cat-file --batch` on blobs.

**Tests heuristic** (stated): a non-merge commit "touches tests" if any changed path matches `(^|/)tests?/|_tests?\.rs$|(^|/)tests?\.rs$|(^|/)testkit/` **or** its `-U0` patch adds a line matching `^\+\s*#\[(test|cfg\(test\))\]` in a `.rs` file. Inline Rust unit tests are therefore caught; edits to existing tests inside non-test-named files without new attributes are not.

### E03-011 — Typical change is small and usually carries tests
- Label: VERIFIED
- Source: `data/E03_size_summary.csv`, `E03_tests_weekly.csv`
- Data: median non-merge commit +52/−5 lines in 2 files; landed (first-parent) changes median +82 in 3 files; 77.5 % of non-merge commits touch tests by the stated heuristic.
- Notes: AI vs non-AI differences in size are small (medians 51 vs 52); not a basis for causal claims.

## Open questions / uncertainties
- Who squash-merged each squash PR and PR open/closed state are not in git (needs GitHub UI/API, blocked; WebFetch spot checks only).
- Model strings in trailers are tool-written self-reports; whether "Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)" vs "Claude Opus 5.5" reflects distinct configurations is unknown.
- 4,199 non-merge commits have no AI attribution — AI use there is unknown, not absent. Several high-volume authors (aiongg, yoriswind, rmsff) have 0 trailers.
- Alias merging is e-mail-based only; residual unmerged aliases are likely (e.g. "Fabio Lissi"/"Fabio Lussi").
- Corrective-activity regexes on subjects are crude; "regression" mixes fixes and regression tests.
- Burst/parallelism metrics cannot separate parallel sessions from batch rebases (author dates survive rebase).
- The 2,238 PR heads with no merge evidence cannot be split into closed/open/superseded from git.
- Why the landing style flipped from squash (W41–W42) to merge commits (W45–W46) is not established.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Machine-readable AI attribution in commit trailers (co-author + session id + model/effort role line) makes AI involvement measurable at scale; here it covers ~50 % of commits (E03-003, E03-004, E03-005).
- Adopting a richer, structured trailer (`Model-Effort:` with driver/briefer/writer roles) late shows the convention can evolve without tooling changes — but only 25 commits use it, so adoption needs enforcement to be useful (E03-005).
- Landing-style choice matters for metrics: squash merges keep main's first-parent history one-change-per-PR; merge commits import sync merges and inflate commit counts 3–4× — pick one and measure on PRs, not commits (E03-001, E03-002).
- A high-throughput, many-contributor AI-assisted project kept typical changes small (median +52/−5, 2 files) and ~78 % of commits touching tests (E03-011).
- Very frequent tagging (median 1.6 days) with a split to a `release` branch once main velocity rose (E03-015).
- Merge-button authority concentrated in very few people despite 582 contributors (E03-008) — a review/integration bottleneck pattern to plan for.
- Agent identities committing under their own name are rare (1 %); attribution mostly flows through human authors with AI trailers, so per-human AI share is the better unit (E03-006, §3 author table).
- "Fix main" clusters after merge waves (E03-013) suggest batch integration needs a post-merge green-main step.
- Docs that agents and humans co-maintain (scorecard, gaps, parity, control protocol) become top hot-spots — budget for doc churn and merge conflicts on them (E03-016).
- Same-identity sub-5-minute commit bursts across unrelated crates are measurable but ambiguous; recording session ids per commit (as `Claude-Session:` does on 238 commits) is what would disambiguate parallel agents (E03-014).

### 0.2 Does the mechanism help agents develop or test PhotoCraft?

Key to the columns:
- **Documented for dev agents**: a primary doc tells developers or agents to use it while building or testing.
- **Observed in history**: commits, tests or PRs show the project using it that way.
- **Hypothesized only**: neither of the above.

## Open questions / uncertainties
- **Exact command count.** The 76 → 805 figures are regex estimates. The exact count needs `photocraft-cli commands`, and the workspace was not built (4 cores, git deps from craft-libs).
- **How often dev agents verify visually.** Only one PR (#7374) was sampled via WebFetch. A second fetch hit a rate limit. Commit messages under-count this practice because AGENTS.md routes screenshots to PR bodies.
- **Squash-merged infrastructure commits.** Many of these carry no trailer (16941f7198, 0f955e6c82, 968baf639e, 74330157cb, …). Whether an agent wrote them is *unknown*, not human.
- **House-rules check.** The shared workflow's logic in craft-common-actions was not inspected.
- **Perf nightly.** Whether the GitHub `macos-15` runner ever matches the baseline machine class (that is, whether the regression gate ever fires) was not checked.
- **`agent_tasks` test count.** The 5+1+1 figure counts `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attributes. The ten tasks may be grouped inside fewer test functions.
- **Thread-count determinism.** No test proving the architecture claim was located.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Make the core headless and enumerable: a registry of JSON commands that tests, the CLI, RPC and MCP all reach. Fuzzing every command becomes a single test (E04-008, E04-010, E04-012).
- Turn architecture rules into cheap CI checks: a dependency-layer linter from day 1, plus a lexical "UI dispatches commands" scanner with a shrink-only allowlist (E04-031, E04-012).
- Give agents a way to *see* the product without a desktop: an offscreen render example that replays control-protocol scripts, and an authenticated control channel with screenshot. Write "verify visually and look at the PNG" into the agent guide (E04-020, E04-021, E04-024).
- Reuse the agent-facing control interface as the UI test driver, so product automation and test automation do not drift apart (E04-023).
- Define "correct" through external oracles: reference-app outputs embedded in files, pinned and hashed corpora, and a CPU reference vs GPU tolerance. Use ratchet floors that are never lowered (E04-036, E04-037, E04-042).
- Keep goals machine-readable and CI-checked: scorecard TOML → generated doc with `--check`; perf budgets with explicit "not measurable, never invent a number" fields (E04-050, E04-051).
- Compile-time completeness tricks (destructuring) stop agents from silently dropping fields in serializers (E04-033).
- Caveat: plan items such as golden images and `xtask bless` were never realised, and no perf budget is enforced. Documented intent is not the same as an active gate (E04-027, E04-051).
- Caveat: the docs drift quickly under high change rates (README, AGENTS.md crate map). Generated docs with `--check` stayed accurate; hand-written ones did not (E04-004, E04-006).

## Open questions / uncertainties
- **Branch protection and required checks**: I could not read them, since the GitHub API is blocked. Check counts (6 → 19–24) and human-approval absence come from WebFetch summaries of 6 PRs only. Whether approvals are required and bypassed, or not required at all, is unknown.
- **E05-003 row "0cc421d0d5"**: I did not verify that sha. The FreeBSD delegation commit observed in the log is `0cc0d0212c7a`? No. The log line is "0cc0…" and I did not re-check it. The verified commits for that change are cddb6fa21c (nix switch, 2026-10-15) and the log line "ci: delegate FreeBSD workflow to craft-common-actions and add nix check" (2026-10-15, Dylan M. Taylor). Treat that row's sha as unverified.
- The contents of the shared `craft-common-actions` workflows (release.yml, house-rules.yml, nix.yml, freebsd.yml) were not read, except the summaries of sonarcloud.yml and gate.yml via WebFetch. Signing, notarization and Flatpak publishing details live there.
- I could not determine whether the nightly perf, FreeBSD, ARM64 and release dry-run jobs are currently green, because I had no Actions access.
- The purpose of the `ci/snapshot-*` branches is undocumented (E05-014, INFERRED).
- The tag-to-tag commit counts use `rev-list prev..tag`, which inflates counts for release-branch tags with merges from main.
- Who published each draft release is not observable.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Make the local gate and the CI gate the **same command** (`cargo xtask ci`), so agents can reproduce CI exactly. Order cheap checks first (E05-010, E05-003 #6119).
- **Never cancel main's CI runs**. Each main state must be verified to the end, or red main becomes invisible under high merge rates (E05-004).
- Without a merge queue, PRs that are each green alone still break main several times a week. Budget for "fix main" work, or add a merge queue (E05-052).
- Turn advisory agent rules into mechanical checks when they matter. panic_hunt, GPU no-skip and panel-commands were all advisory first, then enforced (E05-071, E05-024).
- Make tests **prove they ran**. Reject early-return or skip passes on software adapters (E05-024), and treat zero-match runs as BLOCKED (E05-022, E05-051).
- Prefer root-causing flakes with measured failure rates over retries. A retry policy was tried and dropped (E05-050, E05-053).
- Ratchets (floors, shrinking allowlists, budgets flipped to enforced) let gates tighten without breaking work in progress (E05-072).
- Record CI cost trade-offs, in runner-minutes and slots, next to the config. Path-select expensive platforms, and move slow platforms to nightly (E05-005, E05-013).
- Rotate long test sweeps by day (`Sweep`) to cap per-PR cost while keeping full coverage over a window (E05-021).
- Add nightly release dry runs, so release-only breakage surfaces before release day (E05-063, E05-062).
- Watch for gates that look real but cannot fail: zero enforced perf budgets with a baseline from another machine class (E05-028), a stale fuzz matrix (E05-023), path filters on non-existent files (E05-033), and partial action pinning (E05-009).
- AI review bots (CodeRabbit) are ubiquitous but advisory. On the sampled PRs, human approval was mostly absent. Accountability rests on a written rule, "a person is accountable", rather than a mechanical requirement (E05-030, E05-035).

## Open questions / uncertainties
- Who pressed merge on 2,690 squash merges: git records committer "GitHub". Only the WebFetch sample names mergers.
- Whether the BFlat (+07:00) Claude operator and the bflatastic account are the same person relies on `data/E03_alias_map.csv`. The "same operator ran claude/integ-batch and committed Claude commits" link is INFERRED from tz + committer field.
- How claude/integ-batch-N relates to davidmann4/integration-batch-7..20 (numbering continues, but authors differ). Batches 1–6 of the davidmann4 series were not found on main as merge commits.
- Session counts undercount AI sessions: most AI-attributed commits have no session trailer. Session spans are affected by rebases.
- PR lifetimes use first-commit author date, not PR-open time (not in git). Upper bound on open-to-merge.
- WebFetch summaries may miss review threads on long pages (e.g. #9386 truncated at 100k chars, second part read). Only 4 issue pages and 11 PR pages were sampled (a WebFetch quota interruption cut the sample short).
- The brief's ≈25 `fix/sec-*` and ≈203 Claude-Session commits differ from these counts (20; 274 main commits with a session trailer) because of different counting methods.
- Discussions/wiki/projects pages were not fetched.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Integration trains: bundle N independent PRs into one branch to get one CI run and one conflict-resolution pass, then land by merge commit so the member PRs close themselves (E06-021, E06-022).
- Record conflict resolutions in the merge commit message, file by file with the reasoning (38609e5615, 4365c0537d) (E06-022).
- "CI only (do not merge)" PRs as a cheap combined-test gate before merging members one by one (E06-021).
- Splitting a large agent change by crate into PRs merged back-to-back keeps history reviewable per area, even when nobody reviews the PRs (E06-027).
- Encoding the issue number in the branch name and squash subject (`fix/<issue>-slug`, `Title (#issue) (#PR)`) gives cheap issue→commit traceability. It erodes when merge style changes (E06-031).
- Structural parallel-agent rules (own target dir, new module per feature, atomic manifest writes, wait instead of fixing others' broken files) from day 1 (E06-050).
- Shared generated/tracker files become conflict hot spots under high concurrency. Regenerate them centrally at the integration gate (E06-051, E06-032).
- Label-driven supervision (`ready to merge`, `waiting on author`, `needs decision`) plus bot review (CodeRabbit, Sonar) is how a few maintainers gate hundreds of in-flight PRs (E06-030, E06-041).
- Session trailers (`Claude-Session:`) make agent work countable and traceable per session. Coverage was partial here, which limits their value (E06-011).
- Explicit "who is accountable" rules for agent operators (house rule 1) and a response-time clock (rule 14) are written down, but arrived late (11-06) (E06-041).
- An issue-triage bot that applies labels, links in-progress PRs and flags duplicates keeps a 2,800-issue backlog navigable; epics with "free / being worked on / merged" tables act as claim boards (E06-033, E06-034).
- Branch-name attribution (`codex/*`) can contradict trailers. Use trailers and identity fields as primary (E06-025).

## Open questions / uncertainties
- Reasons for the integration-batch-8 reverts (#9455, #9454, #9183, #4573, #1199) are not in the commits. PR #9386's description was not fetched. This could be checked with WebFetch on pull/9386.
- Whether branch protection requires up-to-date branches. GitHub settings are not visible from git. "(merge queue)" commits suggest a manual practice, not a setting.
- The source tool behind the `Finding: <uuid>` trailers is unnamed.
- Causality for the never-crash trigger (issues #7, #16, #17 → rule 9) is inferred from timing only.
- Fix-type percentages depend on subject conventions that changed (squash → merge commits) in late October. Treat them as indicative only.
- 40/59 fix-main commits carry AI trailers. Absence of a trailer is "unknown", not "human". Since 11-06 house rule 15 discourages attribution in PRs (E02-011), which may depress later trailer rates.
- Original commit d3e8039f76 (reverted by b390bef334) is not in the clone. Δt unknown.
- WebFetch results are small-model summaries (lower fidelity). Quotes from them are short and unverified against raw HTML.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Keep main's CI runs uncancelled. Otherwise red main is invisible. The project lost most of a day's main runs to cancellation (E07-004).
- Expect semantic merge skew to dominate when many agents land in parallel. Use a real or manual merge queue, or staging integration batches. Here, batches coincided with zero red-main commits in W43–W45 (E07-002, E07-003, E07-005).
- Turn agent failure modes into ratcheting metrics instead of prose rules. Examples: "settings that do nothing" 66→8, parity floors (E07-014, E07-013).
- Distrust wiring metrics. "625/625 live" coexisted with broken basics in day-1 user feedback. Pair coverage numbers with behaviour tests (E07-013).
- Make CI fail when tests skip. 57 GPU checks were silently passing on a GPU-less runner (E07-018).
- Ask for "test fails without the fix" evidence and spot-check with mutation. Schedule periodic backfill sweeps for fixes merged without tests (E07-015, E07-018).
- Run a never-crash campaign early as a short, crate-partitioned sweep, backed by deny lints, a command fuzzer and a last-resort guard. Each crash fix carries a test that panicked before (E07-009).
- Put flaky-test fixes in code (locks, process isolation, condition polling) and record before/after failure rates in the commit (E07-007).
- Tightening lint gates mid-flight causes post-merge reds from combinations. Budget for fix-main PRs or check gates in the queue (E07-005, E07-011).
- Avoid "every PR edits the same status line" doc conventions. They create conflict-marker casualties (E07-020).
- Durability fixes need environment-diverse fault injection (SMB, permissions), or they regress real users (E07-021).
- When adding consistency tests for shared catalogs and registries, duplicate entries from parallel work become cheap one-line fixes instead of silent bugs (E07-019).

- HN `echelon` = Brandon Thomas is inferred (same handle as the GitHub login, ownership claims); it is not stated on the profile.
- The scope of the "no human review" remark (E08-016) is unclear.
- Other maintainers were searched only by web search (E08-031). X/Twitter, YouTube (e.g. youtube.com/watch?v=BGShygDux9o cited in HN 50333271; LegalEagle) and Discord were not read directly.
- RFC-0006 and craft-contrib were read only through WebFetch. The RFC's author, date and status are not shown. The `standards/house-rules-*.md` files were not fetched.
- When the GitHub About text dropped "clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop" is unknown (E08-029).

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- State effort in model-specific agent-hours and recalibrate against your own merged-PR history. PhotoCraft did this and revised its estimate about 10× upward within 8 days (E08-002, E08-004, E08-005).
- Write down the parallel-agent mechanics: separate build dirs, file ownership, atomic manifest writes, wait instead of fixing others' breakage (E08-007, E08-020).
- Plan for abrupt session ends with a handoff log and an always-green tree. PhotoCraft keeps that log private, which costs external auditability (E08-007).
- List explicitly the decisions that need a human: licensing, signing, hardware, native-speaker review, checks against the reference app (E08-006).
- Put human accountability per agent run into the house rules (E08-009). Public founder rhetoric ("no human review", E08-016) can undercut that norm.
- Credit models in the product from trailers (E08-010). Note that a later "no agent attribution" rule erodes the same data (E08-008).
- Public "one-shot" and "within a month" claims invite reputational blowback when the project's own docs say alpha (E08-013, E08-019, E08-025). Keep public claims aligned with the in-repo readiness docs.
- Use the community as a distributed token budget. This is a stated strategy (E08-018), and its costs and quality control are undocumented.
- Turn observed agent failure modes into org-wide rules that are copied into each repo with integrity checks. RFC-0006 lists duplicate PRs, already-fixed bugs, abandoned drafts and invented functions, and each rule answers one of them (E08-028, E08-008).
- A clean-room claim needs a documented procedure. "Observed behaviour" here includes reading installed-app resource files and comparing renders (E08-006, E08-017, E08-026).


# E09-case-traces.md

## Open questions / uncertainties
- Review path for the 12 never-crash PRs (#33–#59), #1668, #1533, #195/#224/#190 not fetched (WebFetch budget); "unknown".
- The tool that produced the `Finding:` UUIDs (E09-G-002) is not stated anywhere examined.
- Whether a Codex agent wrote the egui plan rests only on the `codex/` branch prefix and `/home/codex/…` paths (E09-E-001).
- `ebosido444-ai` handle may indicate an AI-operated account; no explicit attribution → unknown (E09-F-004).
- PR #10426 has 7 commits per WF; only 3 are between the merge parents in git (the rest presumably landed with #10425). Not reconciled.
- WF reported #1421 and #9363 as merge commits; git shows single-parent squashes. Git evidence preferred.
- #1248 → 77a258b9a0 follow-up linkage is inferred only.

## Methods-relevant takeaways
- Turn a rule into a counted metric: never-crash deny-attribute coverage is computed by the scorecard (E09-C-003) — transferable as "lint coverage as a tracked number".
- External oracles + ratcheting floors define "correct" for format work without a human judging pixels (E09-D-001, D-002, D-003).
- A campaign can be decomposed into one-commit, per-crate branches landed serially in minutes when each is mechanical (E09-C-004).
- Agent-authored bug fixes carry a fixed message shape (symptom → root cause → behaviour) and a session-link trailer, giving traceability back to the agent session (E09-B-001).
- Same-commit regression tests were the norm but not enforced: #1323 shipped without one, and 16 of 27 security fixes added no `#[test]` (E09-B table, G-003).
- Perf claims are recorded in per-change docs with hardware, method, base-tree reproduction and "what this does not fix"; reviewers caught a harness bug that changed a published number (E09-F-002, F-003).
- Budgets that are not yet met are kept visible as `enforce = false` with a measured note, never deleted (E09-F-004).
- Large migrations used a committed plan with explicit open acceptance gates, and the PR stated what it did not claim (E09-E-001, E-002).
- Post-merge human testing still found semantic gaps in agent-assisted features that had many tests; the follow-up encoded each gap as a named test (E09-H-002, H-003).
- AI bot review (CodeRabbit) was used on most PRs examined and drove real changes (E09-E-002, F-003, H-002), but some PRs merged with no human review and failing checks (E09-B-002).
